title: Regional surge lanes, shadow validation plan, and release train choreographer
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: As we prepare the runtime/console/API rollout for runtime-1.20, we need a coordinated launch calendar that explicitly gates regional surges, formalizes a 'shadow validation' run for downstream consumers, and establishes a single release choreographer role (temporary) to coordinate cross-surface signals. Goal: minimize outage risk and model/regression surprises while enabling predictable capacity ramps and clear rollback criteria.

Scope: this ticket covers planning and runbook for the next release train (runtime + console + API) across NA/EU/APAC: 1) Define 'surge lanes' (timeboxed regional windows with reserved capacity hedges and traffic contracts). 2) Create a shadow validation runbook that automates traffic-shadowing of 10% of production requests to the new runtime variant and surfaces quality/cost delta dashboards. 3) Define release choreographer responsibilities, handoff checklist, and escalation flows for canary, cohort expansion, and rollback. 4) Produce preflight automation templates (capacity checks, observability smoke tests, and embargo windows).

Success metrics:
- No customer-facing SLO regressions >0.5% during cohort expansion.
- Shadow validation detects any model/regression causing >1% difference in critical prompts within first 6 hours.
- Capacity hedges cover 30% extra peak qps during first 48 hours without saturation.
- Documented choreographer runbook used for at least 2 releases in 6 months.

Acceptance criteria:
- Surge lanes calendar published and approved by Runtime, Console, and API leads.
- Shadow validation pipeline implemented end-to-end and wired into Console dashboards.
- Release choreographer role description, rota template, and escalation matrix committed to ops-playbooks.
- Automated preflight checks (capacity, KV cache health, kernel fallback smoke) with pass/fail thresholds in CI.

Deliverables:
- Surge lanes calendar (spreadsheet + calendar invites).
- Shadow validation runbook and a reproducible smoke-suite (GitHub repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-shadow/pull/87).
- Choreographer runbook in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/4123/Release+Choreographer+Runbook.
- Dashboard panels and alerts (Console dashboard link, latency/cost/regression panels).

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Chen (owner)
- Runtime lead: Elena Rivera
- Console lead: Owen Park
- API lead: Priya Nambiar
- Eng on-call rotation managers: Lydia Brooks, Aaron Kim
- SRE: Platform Reliability team

Operational notes and constraints:
- Regional capacity hedges will be purchased as temporary Dedicated capacity reservations where required; finance signoff needed for NA surge (estimate $28k for 48h hedges).
- Shadow validation must mask PII and respect VPC/private deployment constraints; collaborate with Security for dataset scrubbing.
- Canary expansion algorithm: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m stability gate between steps; automated rollback on error budgets or latency spikes above thresholds.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Shadow pipeline adds observable noise and cost. Mitigation: sample 5–10% requests, throttle on cost signal, and only persist minimal traces for flagged regressions.
- Risk: Region-specific infra saturation. Mitigation: preflight capacity stress tests + reserve surge lanes; fallback to a neighboring region per routing policy.

Next steps (short-term):
- 2026-03-05: Align runtime/console/api leads on surge lanes and initial calendar (done).
- 2026-03-08: Draft shadow-validation PR (initial wiring complete, PR#87 opened).
- 2026-03-12: Security and privacy review kickoff scheduled (owner: Priya).
- 2026-03-15: Finalize choreographer job description and propose rota template to Platform SRE (this ticket).

Longer-term:
- Bake shadow validation into continuous release pipelines so every model/service change runs a shadow pass in canary environments before cohort expansion.
- Iterate on surge-lane pricing/hedge playbooks to optimize cost vs. risk.
